name: self-qa
description: Watch a repo's commits, decide which ones a user could notice, and drive one deep as-a-user scenario against the live UI for each — filing an Inbox item and a Task, with a proof bundle, when a scenario fails.

repo.help: Absolute path to the git repository the commits belong to. The commit watcher passes the repo it is configured to watch.

commits.help: New commit SHAs to triage, oldest first. Every one gets a ledger verdict; only the user-impacting ones get a scenario.

base_url.help: Where the running gateway's dashboard is. The scenario drives this instance, so it must be the one built from the commits under test.

fix_branch_enabled.help: On a confirmed failure, open a branch with a proposed diff. Off by default; the branch is never merged and never pushed.

metadata.why_risky: It drives a real browser against your running instance and mutates real state — that is the point, and it is also why it is not something to start without meaning to.
metadata.why_metered: Triage is free and deterministic; only a user-impacting commit spends a scenario, and `agent.self_qa.max_scenarios_per_fire` caps how many one push can start.
metadata.cadence: commit-driven — the commit-watch cron script fires this when the watched repo's HEAD moves, not on a clock.

steering_examples.description: Only check the commit that touched the inbox filters; skip the rest of this push.
The scenario is render-checking rather than mutating state — make it actually send the message and then verify it persisted.

example_outputs: a ledger verdict per commit, and for each user-impacting one a proof bundle plus an Inbox item and Task when the scenario failed

children.label: Which commits could a user notice?
Drive it against the live UI

true.label: Propose a diff on its own branch

false.label: Leave the fix to a human
